'''Allison Beck McCoy''' is an American [[biomedical informatician]] focused on [[clinical informatics]]/[[health informatics]]. She is an associate professor of [[biomedical informatics]] and director of the clinical informatics core at the [[Vanderbilt University School of Medicine]]. She was elected a fellow of the [[American Medical Informatics Association]] and [[American College of Medical Informatics]] in 2018 and 2023 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garchitorena |first=Mia |date=October 17, 2023 |title=Vanderbilt's Ellen Clayton and Allison McCoy elected fellows of ACMI |url=https://news.vumc.org/2023/10/17/vanderbilts-ellen-clayton-and-allison-mccoy-elected-fellows-of-acmi/ |access-date=2024-03-04 |website=Vanderbilt University |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
McCoy obtained a BSCS in computer science at [[Baylor University]] in 2006, and a MS and PhD in biomedical informatics at [[Vanderbilt University]] in 2008 and 2010, respectively.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Allison McCoy, PhD, ACHIP, FACMI, FAMIA {{!}} Department of Biomedical Informatics |url=https://www.vumc.org/dbmi/person/allison-mccoy-phd-achip-facmi-famia |access-date=2024-03-04 |website=www.vumc.org}}</ref> Her master's thesis was titled, ''A System to Monitor and Improve Medication Safety in the Setting of Acute Kidney Injury''.<ref name=":12">{{Cite thesis |last=McCoy |first=Allison Beck |title=A System to Monitor and Improve Medication Safety in the Setting of Acute Kidney Injury |date=2008 |access-date=2024-03-03 |degree=M.S. |publisher=Vanderbilt University |url=https://etd.library.vanderbilt.edu/etd-03312008-085804 |oclc=610018279}}</ref> Lemuel R. Waitman was her thesis advisor.<ref name=":12" /> McCoy's dissertation was titled, ''Achieving Medication Safety during Acute Kidney Injury: The Impact of Clinical Decision Support and Real-Time Pharmacy Surveillance''.<ref name=":22">{{Cite thesis |last=McCoy |first=Allison Beck |title=Achieving Medication Safety during Acute Kidney Injury: The Impact of Clinical Decision Support and Real-Time Pharmacy Surveillance |date=2010 |access-date=2024-03-03 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=Vanderbilt University |url=https://etd.library.vanderbilt.edu/etd-11242010-144036 |oclc=820719175}}</ref> [[Josh F. Peterson]] was her doctoral advisor.<ref name=":22" /> McCoy was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Texas School of Biomedical Informatics under the mentorship of [[Dean F. Sittig]].<ref name=":02" /> She completed [[American Medical Informatics Association|AMIA]] Health Informatics Certification (AHIC) in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AHIC Group |url=https://amia.org/careers-certifications/amia-health-informatics-certification-ahic/achip-diplomates |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=amia.org}}</ref>

== Career ==
McCoy is a biomedical informatician specializing in applied clinical informatics.<ref name=":02" /> She was an assistant professor at the [[University of Texas School of Biomedical Informatics]] and at the [[Tulane University School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine]]'s department of global biostatistics and data science.<ref name=":02" /> McCoy is an associate professor of [[biomedical informatics]] at the [[Vanderbilt University School of Medicine]].<ref name=":02" /> She is the director of its clinical informatics core,<ref name=":02" /> director of research for the Clinical Informatics Research Collaborative (CIRCLE),<ref>{{Cite web |title=CIRCLE: Clinical Informatics Research Collaborative |url=http://circleinformatics.org/ |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=CIRCLE: Clinical Informatics Research Collaborative |language=en-US}}</ref> and director of digital experience for the Pediatric Clinical Decision Support Collaborative (PCC). She created the Biomedical Informatics Ranking Website (Scholar Scraper),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://allisonbmccoy.github.io/scholar-scraper/index-bmi.html |access-date=2024-03-07 |title= Citations Statistics of Biomedical Informatics Researchers|first=Allison|last=McCoy}}</ref> and led the Clickbusters initiative.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Govern |first=Paul |title=Clickbusters program takes on EHR alert fatigue |url=https://news.vumc.org/2020/07/16/clickbusters-program-takes-on-ehr-alert-fatigue/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Vanderbilt University |date=16 July 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

McCoy has published more than 100 papers and has an h-index of 33.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allison B. McCoy, PhD, ACHIP, FACMI, FAMIA |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8fR6ShUAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Allison McCoy is married to Jacob A. McCoy, MD, MS, and they have 2 children. Their son was born with a single ventricle congenital heart defect.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=General 1 |url=https://www.sistersbyheart.org/who-we-are |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Sisters by Heart |language=en-US}}</ref> McCoy is the Director of Scientific Community Engagement for Sisters By Heart.<ref name=":0" /> She is involved with the National Pediatric Quality Improvement Collaborative (NPC-QIC) as a Parent Member of the Scientific Review Committee<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research Overview |url=https://www.npcqic.org/research-overview |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=NPC-QIC |language=en-US}}</ref> and with Fontan Outcomes Network (FON) as the Parent Representative for Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt. She has also served on the Monroe Carell Patient and Family Advisory Council.

McCoy is the daughter of colorectal surgeon [[David E. Beck]].
